( 1 )"], "pediatric_use": ["8.4 Pediatric Use During the induction of anesthesia, saliva flow and tracheobronchial secretion can increase and can be the cause of larynogospasm, particularly in children. Published juvenile animal studies demonstrate that the administration of anesthetic and sedation drugs, such as Isoflurane USP, that either block NMDA receptors or potentiate the activity of GABA during the period of rapid brain growth or synaptogenesis, results in widespread neuronal and oligodendrocyte cell loss in the developing brain and alterations in synaptic morphology and neurogenesis.
